subject: Post-call: hosting path options and compliance evidence needed
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Lina Vargas <lina@cortexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T14:02:00-04:00
Subject: Post-call recap: hosting paths & immediate evidence asks

Lina — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our end: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- Cortex Health will be processing PHI for the planned triage assistant; BAA required.
- Primary preference is to start on Redwood Hosted API for speed-to-prod, but Cortex may require Dedicated capacity or Private VPC depending on procurement/audit outcomes.
- Security team needs SOC 2 Type II, KMS/HSM info, and audit log retention details to close approval.

Our recommended path (short-term / long-term):
1) Short-term: Pilot on Hosted API with tokenized PHI sandboxing and strict collection rules — this gets you live quickly while we run parallel compliance checks.
2) If procurement mandates isolation/pinned throughput or specific SLA, shift to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool).
3) If any regulatory/audit requirement demands customer-controlled network or air-gapped ops, we pursue Private VPC / on-prem option (longer lead).

Immediate asks from your side so we can build a MAP and evidence pack:
- Confirm whether production will include persistent PHI storage or if PHI is ephemeral (in-flight only).
- Share your vendor security questionnaire and any procurement timing constraints.
- Provide point of contact for legal/procurement and for security evidence review.

Attachments: I attached a short hosting comparison + a draft BAA we usually start with (see attachment stubs).

Next steps: I will loop Karthik from infra to map evidence to each hosting path and send a one-page MAP with timeline + deliverables by EOD tomorrow. Please confirm a target procurement review date.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and items from our side: 

1) PHI handling: production will store limited PHI (patient identifiers and short notes) in persistent storage for 30 days for CTR purposes. That means BAA + proof of isolation controls will be required.
2) Timeline: Procurement review window is targeted for the week of Aug 9; security needs evidence earlier (we're hoping to get docs by July 28 to run an internal review).
3) Security asks: please provide your latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted if needed), description of key management (do you support customer-managed keys / HSM?), network segmentation options, and audit-log retention policy.

Attached is our vendor security questionnaire — it is the most efficient way for our security team to evaluate.

Point people: Alyssa Chen (security) and procurement@cortexhealth.com. CC'd them here.

Regards,
Lina Vargas

Date: 2026-07-20T09:04:00-04:00
Subject: Infra evidence mapping for Cortex Health (internal)

Sean / Marissa — following up with a concise technical mapping of what we can deliver per hosting path. Notes below are internal; I'll share an external-friendly version once Lina confirms MAP.

Hosted API (fastest):
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (available), controls matrix mapping (we'll produce), audit-log snapshot (7/19 sample).
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK) and HSM-backed key stores in dedicated deployments.
- Isolation: logical isolation + tenant-level encryption; not physically isolated.

Dedicated capacity (reserved pool):
- Evidence: additional tenancy controls, SLA commitment, dedicated GPU pools, VPC peering options.
- KMS/HSM: support for customer-owned key material via HSM (partner integrations available).

Private VPC / On-prem:
- Evidence: network diagrams, on-prem deployment checklist, on-site audit support (subject to SOW).
- Lead time: 8-12 weeks for on-prem packaging and installation.

Deliverables I can produce by Jul 20 EOD (external-ready):
- infra-fit-analysis.pdf (controls mapping per hosting path)
- a redlined BAA and a checklist that ties each control to a document or artifact we can produce.

Questions:
- Do we need full SOC 2 report delivery to Alyssa or will a redacted copy + controls matrix suffice for the initial review?

Attachment: infra-fit-analysis.pdf (pdf stub)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
